resources.string: Your passwords are never uploaded or sent anywhere. PassVault checks them here, on this device, and nothing leaves it. Because it works offline, it cannot look passwords up in online lists of leaked passwords.
The same password on several sites: one leak exposes them all.
Easy to guess. Replace them with generated ones.
Not changed for over a year.
Expired, or expiring within the next 30 days.
Well-known services with no 2FA code saved in PassVault. If you already use another authenticator or text messages for them, ignore this.

PassVault keeps no cloud copy: if this phone is lost or reset, only your own backups bring your entries back. A reminder appears in the app when a backup is due and something has changed. CSV exports do not count, because they leave out 2FA keys, seed phrases, cards and notes.
No backup yet. If this phone is lost or reset, these entries are gone.
Enter the database password. If it also uses a key file, choose it too. Opening it can take a few seconds.

A second app password that opens a separate, harmless vault. If someone forces you to unlock PassVault, enter the decoy password: they see only what you put in the decoy vault, and your real entries stay hidden.\n\nTo fill it, lock PassVault and unlock with the decoy password. This setting is not shown inside the decoy vault. Biometric unlock always opens your real vault, so turn it off if you might be made to use it. Someone who knows PassVault well and examines the phone\'s storage could still tell that a second vault exists.
Decoy vault set up. Lock PassVault and unlock with the decoy password to fill it.
This deletes the decoy vault and everything in it. Your real vault is not affected.
Your decoy vault is set up. You can give it a new password, for example if you forgot it; what is in it is kept. Removing it deletes it and everything in it.
Enter your app password, then a new password for the decoy vault. Its entries are kept.
This decoy vault was set up by an earlier test version, so its password cannot be changed from here. Remove it and set it up again.
Moving QR code or a file, no network needed
Enter your app password. PassVault then shows a moving QR code for the new phone to scan, and a one-time transfer code to type there.
Scan the moving QR code on the old phone
On the new phone, open PassVault, go to Settings, Receive from another phone, and point its camera at this screen. Keep this screen open until it is done.
Type this code on the new phone when it asks. The QR codes hold only encrypted data; without this code they are useless, so don\'t let anyone photograph it.
Transfer file saved. On the new phone, import it and type the transfer code.
This vault is too large for QR codes. Save a transfer file instead.
Point the camera at the moving QR code on the old phone. Codes can arrive in any order; missed ones come round again.
Enter the transfer code shown on the other phone.
Leaving PassVault to send the file locks it. Unlock again within 10 minutes and this screen comes back with the same code.
